title: Smart Thermostat Rebates in Pasadena 2026: $50 from PWP | HomePowerRebate
desc: Pasadena Water and Power pays $50 for a Wi-Fi smart thermostat, $10 more for buying in Pasadena and a $50 bonus on assistance. Limits, paperwork and fit tips.
lead: Pasadena Water and Power pays $50 for a Wi-Fi smart thermostat, with a photo of the finished install as part of the proof. It is the quickest rebate on the list and the one most likely to be worth doing alongside a bigger project.
cards_heading: What Pasadena Water and Power pays
cards_intro: These figures come from PWP's smart thermostat page, which we read on October 2, 2026. Only residential PWP electric customers qualify.

cards.title: Base rebate
cards.note: For a new Wi-Fi enabled smart thermostat that you install in your home.

cards.title: Bought in Pasadena
cards.note: Added when you buy the thermostat from a seller in Pasadena.

cards.title: Bill Payment Assistance
cards.note: For customers enrolled in PWP's income-qualified Bill Payment Assistance program.

after_cards:
The math

One thermostat bought in Pasadena earns $50 + $10 = $60. A customer on Bill Payment Assistance can add $50 per unit, and with two thermostats that comes to as much as $220 over five years if everything stacks. PWP does not spell out the stacking, so ask before you count on it.
sections: Burbank pays up to $75 for a smart thermostat (Burbank thermostat rebates). Southern California Edison customers can get a $75 bill credit for enrolling a thermostat in demand response, which is a different kind of offer. Glendale's current rebate list has no thermostat rebate at all. So Pasadena's $50 sits in the middle, and it is paid as a check after you buy, not as a credit for joining a program.
Your utility: Pasadena Water and Power

PWP pays this one, and only for PWP electric customers. Pasadena gas customers can also look at the Southern California Gas Company, which PWP's page names as a source of additional rebates. Gas company offers change often, so check its rebate page the week you buy. We did not read the SoCalGas page and cannot quote an amount.
Check that it works with your system

A smart thermostat only helps if it fits your heating and cooling equipment. Heat pumps, multi-stage systems and old wall furnaces each have different needs. Check that the model supports your system type, and check whether your system already has a common wire (a C-wire) at the thermostat. Take a photo of the old wiring before you remove anything, because PWP also wants a photo of the finished install for the rebate.

Pasadena winters are mild, with an average January low of 7.5°C (about 45°F) over 2015 to 2024, so a heating schedule saves less here than in a cold city. Make sure the model you buy handles cooling well, and use its schedule for the hours the house is empty.

PWP asks for your complete sales receipt or paid invoice showing the product and model number, the date purchased and installed or delivered, and a proof-of-install photo. Rebates are for new products only, not refurbished ones. Apply within 180 days of the purchase date, and keep the order confirmation if you bought online.
installers_intro: A thermostat is a do-it-yourself job for some homes and an installer job for others, especially with a heat pump or a multi-stage system. These Pasadena-area HVAC companies have the best Google ratings, listed by rating and then review count. We are not paid to list anyone.
claim_heading: How to claim the PWP rebate
claim_steps: Check that PWP is your electric utility. The name is on your electric bill.
Buy a new Wi-Fi enabled smart thermostat. Buy it from a Pasadena seller if you want the extra $10.
Install it, and take a photo of the finished install.
Log in to your PWP account and choose Apply for Rebate. Upload the receipt or paid invoice with the model number, the dates, and the install photo.
Apply within 180 days of the purchase date.
PWP says the check arrives 6 to 8 weeks after approval.
faq: How much is the smart thermostat rebate in Pasadena?
$50, plus $10 if you buy in Pasadena. Customers on PWP's Bill Payment Assistance program can add $50 per unit.
How many thermostats can I claim?
PWP limits the rebate to two thermostats every five years.
Do I need approval before I buy?
No. PWP pays after the install. Apply within 180 days of the purchase date.
A complete receipt or paid invoice with the model number and dates, and a photo of the installed thermostat.
Will a smart thermostat save much in Pasadena?
It depends on your system and habits. Winters here are mild, so most of the gain comes from cooling and from not conditioning an empty house.
